newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt to face 23rd confidence vote Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt to face 23rd confidence vote Wednesday.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government on Tuesday called a parliamentary confidence vote for the 23rd time in its year of office, to opposition anger.
Public Works Minister Paolo Costa formally called the vote in the lower house of parliament to overcome amendments threatening a decree on state building projects.
House speaker Luciano Violante said the vote would be held on Wednesday evening after 1630 GMT.

The vote should sweep away hundreds of amendments tabled by the separatist Northern League, whose obstructive tactics forced the government to call a confidence motion last week on a similar decree regarding Albanian refugees in Italy.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government relies on the support of the hard-left Communist Refoundation in the lower house for a majority but is not seen in danger in the vote which is a technical measure to prevent a decree lapsing.
Under a constitutional court ruling, decrees passed by the cabinet have a 60-day life and must be either passed by parliament within that time or lapse.

The construction decree, to create special authorities to streamline the approval process for starting or resuming public works that have been long frozen or stalled, must be approved by the lower house by May 25.
By calling a confidence vote, the approval process is speeded up because blocking amendments are swept away and the house votes on a package with a simple yes or no vote.
If the government loses, it falls.
Far-right National Alliance deputy Maurizio Gasparri said the government's repeated use of such votes was undemocratic and silenced parliamentary debate.
He called Prime Minister Romano Prodi a "Little Stalin... who through confidence votes and arrogance prevents the parliament from freely expressing itself."
Rocco Buttiglione, leader of the small centre-right CDU party, said that the government lost a "little piece of credibility" every time it carried out a confidence vote
"And every time it does it, it carries out another violation of parliament."

The centre-left coalition in turn said it would present a dossier on Wednesday exposing the opposition's obstructionism and how such tactics had affected parliamentary business in the year since the government came to power.

The League, which last year proclaimed the symbolic independence of northern Italy, has taken to obstructing most government decrees with a barrage of amendments, in a bid to snarl parliamentary activity.
League deputy Pierluigi Copercini had earlier called the decree "hogwash -- a sewn-up, cobbled-together law" and challenged the government to call a confidence vote.
The upper house has already approved the measure, of particular importance to impoverished southern Italy where unemployment is high.
Many construction projects throughout Italy have been frozen for years since a corruption scandal exposed by graft-busting magistrates swept away Italy's old political order in 1992.
Some such projects have been exposed as lucrative sources of kickbacks and bribes from contractors.
